paragraphs.en: THE THREE GODFATHERS
paragraphs.zh: 教父三部曲

paragraphs.en: By Peter B. Kyne
paragraphs.zh: 作者：彼得·B·凯恩

paragraphs.en: Illustrated By Dean Cornwell
paragraphs.zh: 由迪恩·科尔内尔绘制插图

paragraphs.en: Cosmopolitan Book Corporation, New York
paragraphs.zh: 《时尚》图书公司，纽约

paragraphs.en: _Is the story of The Three Bad Men---not The Three Wise Men “What's a godfather, Bill?” The Youngest Bad Man inquired. “What job does he hold down?”_
paragraphs.zh: “《三个坏人》的故事——不是《三博士来朝》。‘比尔，教父是什么？”最小的坏人问道。“他做什么工作？”

paragraphs.en: _“You're an awful ignorant young man, Bob,” replied The Wounded Bad Man reproachfully. “A godfather is a sort of reserve parent who promises to renounce the devil with all his works an' pomps.”_
paragraphs.zh: “你真是个粗鄙的年轻人，鲍勃，”受伤的坏人责备地说，“教父是一种后备父母，他发誓要弃绝魔鬼及其一切虚荣和浮华。”

paragraphs.en: _The Youngest Bad Man smiled wanly. “Well, Bill, all I got to say is that us three're a lovely bunch o' godfathers.”_
paragraphs.zh: “最小的坏蛋苦笑着说道：‘好吧，比尔，我只能说我们三个是一群很棒的教父。’”

paragraphs.en: THE THREE GODFATHERS
paragraphs.zh: 教父三部曲

paragraphs.en: THE daylight raid on the Wickenburg National Bank had not been a success. It had been well planned, boldly and cleverly executed, and the four bandits had gathered unto themselves quite a fortune in paper money; the job had been singularly free from fuss and feathers. Nevertheless, as has already been stated, the raid was not a success. The assistant cashier, returning from luncheon, had, from a distance of half a block, observed two strangers in town. Both strangers were mounted and stood on guard in front of the Wickenburg National. In an alley just back of the bank two saddle horses were standing; and as the assistant cashier paused, irresolute, two men came out of the bank, mounted the two horses waiting in the alley, and, followed by the men who had been standing on watch in front of the bank, rode out of Wickenburg in rather a suspicious hurry. The assistant cashier had an inspiration.
paragraphs.zh: 白天对维肯伯格国家银行的突袭并没有成功。这次行动计划周密，大胆而巧妙地实施，四名强盗为自己攫取了一大笔纸币；这次行动异常顺利，没有丝毫混乱和麻烦。然而，正如已经提到的，这次突袭并没有成功。当班的出纳员在午饭后返回时，从一个街区之外的距离，看到有两个陌生人出现在镇上。这两个陌生人都骑着马，站在维肯伯格国家银行前面警戒。在银行后面的一条小巷里，有两匹备好鞍的马。 站在那里；当助理出纳员犹豫不决地停住时，有两个人从银行里走了出来，骑上了小巷里等待的两匹马，随后跟着那些一直在银行前面站岗的男子，他们匆忙地骑马离开了维肯伯格。助理出纳员突然有了一个想法。

paragraphs.en: “Thieves! Robbers! Stop 'em!” he yelled.
paragraphs.zh: “小偷！强盗！拦住他们！”他喊道。

paragraphs.en: His hue and cry aroused to action an apparently inoffensive and elderly citizen who was taking his siesta in front of The Three Deuces saloon. Now this man in front of The Three Deuces was not the sheriff. He was not even the city marshal. Rather he inclined one to the belief that he might be a minister of the gospel--a soul-trapper on guard at the portals of The Three Deuces, within which, judging by the subdued rattle of poker chips, ivory balls and an occasional hoarse shout of “Keno!” one could be reasonably certain of a plethora of brands ripe for the burning. The aged citizen asleep in the chair outside was arrayed in somber black, with a turn-down collar and white lawn tie, a “biled” shirt with a ruby stud in it, and patriarchial white whiskers. But his coat, of a clerical cut, effectually concealed two pieces of artillery of a style and caliber popularized by time and tradition in the fair state of Arizona.
paragraphs.zh: 他的呼喊引起了一位看似无害、年迈的市民的注意，此人正在“三双”酒吧前午睡。这位站在“三双”酒吧前的人并不是警长，甚至也不是市警察局长。他倒更让人觉得可能是一位传教士——一个灵魂捕手，守在“三双”酒吧的门口。从里面传来的低声的扑克牌碰撞声、象牙球的响动声，以及偶尔的一声嘶哑的“开彩啦！”可以合理地推测，里面充斥着大量等待被烧毁的劣质酒。这位正在午睡的年迈市民 外面的椅子上坐着一个人，穿着庄重的黑色衣服，领子翻下来，系着一条白亚麻领带，一件“biled”衬衫，领口别着一颗红宝石胸针，留着父权式的白色胡须。但他那件教士式样的外套下，却藏了两件武器，这种款式和规格在亚利桑那州这个公正的州里，早已被时间和传统所推崇。

paragraphs.en: The four galloping horsemen were abreast The Three Deuces when the cry of “Robbers!” aroused all Wickenburg. It awoke the man in the chair; and he came to his feet with the suddenness of a ferocious old dog, filled both hands and cut loose at one of the four horsemen. There was a reason for this. The elderly citizen had a deposit of three dollars and seventeen cents in the Wickenburg National. Also he possessed a fair proportion of civic pride, and the horseman upon whom he trained his hardware was carrying a gunny-sack containing a pro rata of the said elderly citizen's three-seventeen.
paragraphs.zh: 四名骑马的歹徒与“三双”酒吧并排而过时，有人喊道：“强盗！”这声音惊动了整个维肯伯格镇。这声音惊醒了坐在椅子上的那个人，他像一只凶猛的老狗一样猛地站起身来，双手握紧武器，朝四名骑马的歹徒中的一人开火。他这样做的原因是有道理的。这位年长的市民在维肯伯格国家银行存了三美元十七美分。此外，他也有相当一部分的公民荣誉感，而他瞄准的那名骑马人所背的麻袋里，装着这位年长市民那三美元十七美分中相应比例的钱。

paragraphs.en: Four Bad Men had ridden into Wickenburg that December afternoon, but only three rode out. One of the three had a bullet hole through his left shoulder. The man who stayed lay, thoroughly and effectually defunct, on top of a bulging gunny-sack in front of The Three Deuces. Came presently the paying teller of the Wickenburg National and removed the gunny-sack. Came half an hour later the coroner of Wickenburg and removed the body. As for the elderly citizen of deceptive appearance, he walked uptown to a hardware store, replenished his supply of ammunition and returned to The Three Deuces in a highly cheerful frame of mind. Here let us leave him, for with this story he has nothing further to do. From now on our interest must center on The Three Bad Men who rode out of Wickenburg headed for the California line--which happens to be the Colorado River.
paragraphs.zh: 12月的那天下午，四个恶棍骑马来到了维肯伯格，但只有三人骑马离开了。其中一人左肩中了子弹。那个留下的人则彻底、有效地死去了，倒在“三双靴子”酒吧前面一个鼓鼓的麻袋上。不久，维肯伯格国家银行的出纳员来了，拿走了那个麻袋。半小时后，维肯伯格的法医也来了，把尸体搬走了。至于那个外表看似年长的市民，他走到市区的一家五金店，补充了他的弹药，然后返回了“三双靴子”酒吧。 心情非常愉快。此刻我们就让他留在这里吧，因为这个故事他已经不再参与了。从现在开始，我们的兴趣必须集中在那三个坏人身上，他们从维肯堡出发，前往加利福尼亚州边界——那正好是科罗拉多河。

paragraphs.en: They made their first halt at Granite Tanks, twenty-five miles from Wickenburg. Here they watered their horses and then pressed onward toward the river. At the river they found a boat, thoughtfully provided for just such an emergency as the present.
paragraphs.zh: 他们在距离维肯伯格25英里的花岗岩水槽处第一次停下休息。在这里，他们给马匹饮水，然后继续向河边进发。在河边，他们发现了一艘船，显然是为这种紧急情况特意准备的。

paragraphs.en: Darkness had already settled over the land when The Three Bad Men came to the Colorado River. It would have been wise on their part to have waited until the rising of the moon, but our story does not deal with The Three Wise Men. Within the hour a posse might appear, and, moreover, The Three Bad Men were of that breed that prefers to “take a chance.” They rode their jaded horses into the flood until the yellow waters lapped their bellies; then they shot them and shoved the carcasses off into the current.
paragraphs.zh: 当“三恶人”来到科罗拉多河时，黑暗早已笼罩了大地。对他们来说，明智的做法是等到月亮升起再行动，但我们的故事并不涉及“三智人”。一小时内，可能会有一队追捕者出现，而且“三恶人”正是那种喜欢“碰运气”的人。他们骑着疲惫的马匹进入泛滥的河水中，直到黄色的河水漫到马腹处；然后他们开枪打死了马，把尸体推入了激流中。

paragraphs.en: An hour later The Three Bad Men landed on the California side near Bill Williams Mountain, filled their boat with stones and sank it, and shouldering a supply of food and water sufficient to last them four days, headed up a long box canon that led north to the Colorado Desert. They made fair time after the moon came up. All night long they trudged through the box canon, and at daylight it opened out into the waste.
paragraphs.zh: 一小时后，三恶人降落在比尔·威廉姆斯山附近的加州一侧，他们往船上装满石头后将其沉没，然后背上足以维持四天的食物和水，向一条通往科罗拉多沙漠北部的长峡谷进发。月亮升起后，他们行进得相当顺利。整夜他们都在峡谷中跋涉，天亮时，峡谷豁然开朗，展现在他们面前的是一片荒原。

paragraphs.en: “Well, boys, I guess we're safe.” remarked The Worst Bad Man, who was the leader of the trio. “It's cooler in the canon, so suppose we camp here. I feel like breakfast and some sleep. How's your shoulder, Bill?”
paragraphs.zh: “好吧，伙计们，我想我们安全了。”最坏的坏人——这三个人的头目说道，“炮管里更凉快，我们在这里扎营吧。我想吃早饭，然后睡一觉。比尔，你的肩膀怎么样？”

paragraphs.en: The Wounded Bad Man shrugged the wounded member disdainfully.
paragraphs.zh: 受伤的坏蛋不屑地耸了耸受伤的那只手。

paragraphs.en: “High up. Missed the bone and don't amount to much, Tom. But I've bled like a stuck pig and it's weakened me a little.”
paragraphs.zh: “高处。没击中骨头，也没什么大不了的，汤姆。但我已经像被宰的猪一样流了很多血，这让我有点虚弱。”

paragraphs.en: “I'll heat some water and wash it up, Bill,” said The Youngest Bad Man, much concerned.
paragraphs.zh: “我来烧点水把它洗一洗，比尔，”最年轻的坏蛋说，他非常担心。

paragraphs.en: They made a very small fire of cat-claw and ironwood, brewed a pot of coffee, breakfasted, washed and dressed The Wounded Bad Man's shoulder and slept until late afternoon. They awoke much refreshed, ate an early supper and struck out across the desert to the north, where in time they would come to the Santa Fe tracks. There were lonely stations out there in the sands--they might be worth investigation. Then on to the new mining camp at Old Woman Mountain--a camp which, following the whimsical and fantastic system of desert nomenclature, which seems to trend toward such names as Mecca, Cadiz. Bagdad, Bengal and Siam, had had bestowed upon it the not inappropriate name of New Jerusalem.
paragraphs.zh: 他们用猫爪树和铁木生起了一小堆火，煮了一壶咖啡，吃了早饭，洗漱穿衣，包扎了受伤的坏人肩膀，然后一直睡到下午晚些时候。他们醒来时精神好多了，吃了早饭，便向北边的沙漠出发，最终他们会到达圣达菲铁路线。那里有孤零零的车站，隐藏在沙海中——或许值得去探查一下。接着他们前往老妇人山的新采矿营地——这个营地的命名遵循着荒漠地名中那种荒诞而奇特的体系，这种体系似乎倾向于使用麦加、卡迪兹之类的名称。 巴格达、孟加拉和暹罗，曾给它一个颇为贴切的称号，即“新耶路撒冷”。

paragraphs.en: For a number of reasons The Three Bad Men preferred to travel by night. Primarily they were prowlers and preferred it. Secondly, although one may encounter torrid weather by day on the Colorado Desert even in December, the nights, on the contrary, are bitterly cold--and The Three Bad Men had no blankets. Also there was this advantage about traveling at night and sleeping in the shadow of a rock by day: they would not meet other wanderers and there would he no embarrassing questions to answer respecting the hole in The Wounded Bad Man's shoulder.
paragraphs.zh: 出于多种原因，三个恶棍更喜欢夜间行进。首先，他们本来就是夜行的匪徒，喜欢这样。其次，尽管在十二月的科罗拉多沙漠白天可能会遇到酷热的天气，但夜晚却异常寒冷——而三个恶棍没有毯子。此外，夜间行进、白天躲在岩石阴影里休息还有一个好处：他们不会遇到其他流浪者，也不会被问及有关受伤的恶棍肩膀上那个洞的问题。

paragraphs.en: Consequently The Three Bad Men traveled by night. From Mojave Tanks they swung west to avoid the mining operations there, although more than once they glanced back wistfully at the little cluster of yellow lights shining across the sands. The Wounded Bad Man's shoulder was in a bad way and needed medical attention. Also they needed water; but they were desert-bred and could last until they came to Malapai Springs.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，三个坏人选择在夜间行进。他们从莫哈韦水槽出发，向西行进以避开那里的采矿作业，尽管他们不止一次依依不舍地回头望向那片沙地上闪烁着的小小一片黄光。受伤的坏人肩膀伤势严重，需要医疗救助。此外，他们也需要水；但他们是沙漠中长大的，能够坚持到到达马拉帕伊泉。

paragraphs.en: So they turned their backs on Mojave Tanks and tramped onward. Now they were in the ghostly moonlight of the open desert, with the outlines of the mountain ranges on each side looming dim and shadowy fifteen or twenty miles away; now they were picking their way carefully through clusters of murderous catclaw, through tangles of mesquit and ironwood. Up dark, lonely arroyos they went; down long alleys between the outstretched arms of the ocatillas with their pendulous, blood-red blossoms, passing dried, withered Joshua trees twisted into fantastic shapes as if their fearful surroundings had caused them to writhe in horror; through solitude and desolation so vast and profound as to inspire one with the thought that the Creator, appalled at the magnitude of this abortion of Nature, had set it apart as an eternal heritage of the damned.
paragraphs.zh: 于是他们背弃了莫哈韦水箱，继续向前行进。此刻他们置身于开阔荒野中幽灵般的月光下，两侧山峦的轮廓在十五到二十英里之外显得模糊而阴森；他们现在正小心地穿行在致命的猫爪丛中，穿过荆棘丛生的滨藜和铁木林。他们沿着黑暗而荒凉的沟壑向上攀爬；穿过仙人掌枝条伸展如手臂之间长长的通道，那些仙人掌开着下垂的、血红色的花朵，他们经过干枯枯萎的约书亚树，这些树扭曲成奇特的形状，仿佛它们可怕的环境所造成的。 使他们惊恐万分地扭动着；那种孤独与荒凉如此广袤而深沉，以至于让人想到，造物主因对大自然这一畸形产物的规模感到震惊而将其隔离出来，作为堕落者永恒的遗产。

paragraphs.en: In the forenoon of the fifth day they came to Malapai Springs. Here The Three Bad Men drank deeply, bathed, filled their canteens and stepped blithely out for Terrapin Tanks, the next water-hole--a little-known and consequently unfrequented spot--where they could rest for a few days before attempting the last desperate leg of their journey to the railroad.
paragraphs.zh: 在第五天的上午，他们来到了马拉派泉。在这里，三个恶人痛饮了一番，洗了澡，灌满了水囊，然后轻松地出发前往下一个水源——陆龟池。那是一个鲜为人知、因而人迹罕至的地方，他们可以在那里休息几天，然后再踏上最后那段绝望的旅程，前往铁路。

paragraphs.en: “Don't stint yourself on the water. Bill,” The Worst Bad Man advised as they departed from Malapai Springs. “There's always water at Terrapin Tanks.” Nevertheless, with the instinct of the desert-bred, The Worst Bad Man and The Youngest Bad Man were sparing with the water themselves, although careful to conceal this fact from The Wounded Bad Man. The latter's shoulder was swollen and inflamed, and it was a relief to him if the bandages were kept wet.
paragraphs.zh: “别舍不得喝水，比尔，”最坏的坏人临别时对他说，“在陆龟水坑那儿总是有水的。”尽管如此，凭着沙漠出生的本能，最坏的坏人和最小的坏人自己却很节省用水，尽管他们小心地不让受伤的坏人察觉这一点。后者肩膀肿胀发炎，如果绷带保持湿润对他来说是一种安慰。
